rationale: Step 4 ran successfully (replication_log.json, exit_code 0) and wrote results/table2_and_regionyear.json, whose region_year block gives census_division_share=0.6419 (64%) and census_region_share=0.5704 (57%). The paper reports about 38% common to Census divisions and about 26% common to Census regions. The produced values are far outside the bands: |64.2-38|/38 = 69% and |57.0-26|/26 = 119% relative error, both well beyond the 30% partial threshold. The discrepancy has a clear methodological cause visible in src/state_national_elasticities.py: r2_group is applied to raw annual Δln state employment (dln_emp) regressed on region-year dummies, so the national year component (reported separately as national_year_share=0.452) is folded into each R^2. The paper's figures are shares of *relative* (state-minus-national) employment variation, i.e. the national fluctuation should be removed first; netting it out (e.g. (0.642-0.452)/(1-0.452)=0.35, (0.570-0.452)/(1-0.452)=0.21) would land near the paper's numbers, but the run did not produce those values — the emitted evidence is 64% and 57%. Grading the produced result, it does not match.
